profiles.title: Pentecost: The Descent of the Holy Spirit
profiles.subject: Feasts

overview.text: Bishop Joachim of Amissos explains Pentecost as the descent of the Holy Spirit fifty days after the Resurrection. His published account relates the apostles’ languages and teaching to the Church’s proclamation and the prophecy of Joel.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: In the type he describes, the apostles sit on a curved bench beneath rays and tongues of fire. Peter and Paul occupy leading places. The crowned figure below personifies the world in darkness, receiving the apostles’ teaching represented by twelve scrolls.
blocks.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: The selected historic Novgorod image is titled The Descent of the Holy Spirit in its file record. Its semicircular apostolic assembly and lower crowned figure correspond to the type discussed in Bishop Joachim’s account; it is not the new Saint Nicholas Shrine artwork.

blocks.text: The bishop stresses that the composition depicts the Church’s fullness rather than a photographic record: Paul, Mark, and Luke can appear although not all belonged to the original Twelve. The central place belongs to Christ, the Church’s Head.

blocks.text: And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
